title: Training, Validation, and Test Datasets
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose of training, validation, and test sets.
Choose split strategies that match deployment.
Identify leakage through features, preprocessing, and repeated entities.

mentalModel.text: Training teaches the model, validation helps select models and settings, and test estimates final performance after the design is frozen. If test results influence your choices, the test set is no longer an independent final check.

blocks.text: A model can look excellent offline and fail in production if evaluation accidentally includes future information, duplicate entities, or preprocessing fitted on all rows.

concepts.title: Technical deep dive and worked example

blocks.text: Split strategy should match what must be new at deployment. Forecasting usually needs time-respecting splits; repeated customers or patients often need group splits. Fit learned preprocessing on training data only.

blocks.problem: A dataset contains 20 visits per patient, and the model will be used on patients it has never seen.
reasoning: A random row split can put the same patient's patterns in training and test.
Split by patient ID so all visits for a patient stay in one partition.
Fit preprocessing on training patients only and reserve an untouched final test set.
blocks.outcome: Split on the unit that must be new at deployment, not automatically on individual rows.

blocks.source:
from sklearn.model_selection import GroupShuffleSplit
splitter = GroupShuffleSplit(test_size=0.2, n_splits=1, random_state=42)
train_idx, test_idx = next(splitter.split(X, y, groups=patient_ids))
X_train, X_test = X.iloc[train_idx], X.iloc[test_idx]
print(len(set(patient_ids[train_idx]) & set(patient_ids[test_idx])))
blocks.title: Keep patient groups separate

blocks.text: Expected output: 0 — no patient ID appears in both partitions. This assumes pandas-like X/y and indexable patient_ids.
A single split is simple but noisy. Cross-validation costs more but can give a more stable estimate. Time/group splits may reduce sample size yet better reflect deployment.
Production check: For churn forecasting, train on earlier periods and evaluate on later ones. Monitor performance after launch because production data may still drift.

blocks.title: Anti-pattern to avoid
blocks.content: Tuning on test results; splitting rows when users repeat; fitting preprocessing on all rows; random splitting a future-forecasting task.

blocks.text: 1. Problem and motivation — A model can look excellent offline and fail in production if evaluation accidentally includes future information, duplicate entities, or preprocessing fitted on all rows.

2. Definition and design choice — Split strategy should match what must be new at deployment. Forecasting usually needs time-respecting splits; repeated customers or patients often need group splits. Fit learned preprocessing on training data only.

3. Internal mechanism — Split first using the deployment-appropriate strategy; fit preprocessing and model parameters on training data; use validation for selection; use test only after design decisions are frozen.

blocks.outcome: Split on the unit that must be new at deployment, not automatically on individual rows.

blocks.text: 4. Trade-offs and scale — A single split is simple but noisy. Cross-validation costs more but can give a more stable estimate. Time/group splits may reduce sample size yet better reflect deployment.
5. Anti-patterns — Tuning on test results; splitting rows when users repeat; fitting preprocessing on all rows; random splitting a future-forecasting task.
6. Interview probes — What must be unseen at deployment? When does random splitting fail? Which transformations learn from data? How do you prevent selecting on the test set?

tradeoffsAndPitfalls.title: Engineering rule of thumb
tradeoffsAndPitfalls.content: Use the split that simulates how the model will actually be used.

interviewScenarios.prompt: A model achieves 99% offline accuracy but fails in production. What do you inspect first?
strongAnswerPoints: Audit prediction-time feature availability and target leakage.
Check duplicate entities and preprocessing scope.
Compare offline and production populations and label definitions.
pitfalls: Assuming the model simply needs more parameters
interviewScenarios.referenceAnswer: I would audit leakage and split design, then compare feature availability and production distribution. I would verify that preprocessing was fitted only on training data and repeated entities did not cross partitions.

interviewScenarios.prompt: A medical model must generalize to unseen patients. How do you evaluate it?
strongAnswerPoints: Split by patient ID, not visit row.
Keep every visit for a patient in one partition.
pitfalls: Randomly splitting visits and claiming new-patient generalization
interviewScenarios.referenceAnswer: I would use a patient-grouped split. That tests generalization to unseen patients rather than recognition of familiar patient-specific patterns.
